_canon: canon.md, sections Era and Brands and law
_note: The four minted entries are RECORDED from canon.md, not invented here. Renaming one is a canon violation, not an edit.

brands.name: Meridian Town AFC
brands.register: the Town, or just Town. Nobody says the full name except the paper and the announcer.
brands.physical: Ashlar Lane ground: one covered stand, three open sides, a corrugated end that drums in rain. Blue and white halves on scarves in pub windows and on the back shelf of cars. A club shop that is a portacabin open two hours on a Saturday.
brands.says: The town had money once and spent it on a stand. Fourth tier, one promotion in living memory, a cup run in 1979 that men still date things from.
brands.neverConfuse: Any real English club. There is no Meridian in the league pyramid and the name is chosen because it is a harbour word, not a place name borrowed from anywhere.

brands.name: The Meridian Argus
brands.register: the Argus. Older people say the local. A copy is a paper, never a newspaper.
brands.physical: Broadsheet masthead in blackletter over a front page that is two thirds photograph. Yellow vendor boards chained to lamp posts with one line hand-marked in marker. A first edition on the stands by two, a late edition with the results by six.
brands.says: This is where the town finds out what happened to it. Court reports, planning notices, deaths, and the harbour tonnage. If the Argus has not printed a thing, it did not officially happen.
brands.neverConfuse: Any real regional title. Argus is a common enough name for a paper that the qualifier does the work: it is always The Meridian Argus in print.

brands.name: Radio Tideline
brands.register: Tideline. On air the presenters say this is Tideline, and never the word radio twice.
brands.physical: A transmitter cabled to a tower block roof on the Barrows estate and moved when the vans come. A phone-in on a landline with the number read out slowly and twice. Stickers on van doors and inside bus shelters. No premises anybody admits to.
brands.says: Somebody in this town wanted a voice enough to break the law for it. Soul and dub after dark, the football phone-in on Saturday, and small ads for cash work read out as favours.
brands.neverConfuse: Any real pirate station of the period. The name is a harbour word, and no real broadcaster is referenced, sampled or named on air.

brands.name: Coastway Television
brands.register: Coastway. The regional news programme is Coastway Tonight, said in full because that is how the announcer says it.
brands.physical: A rotating station ident in blue and grey. Outside-broadcast van with the logo on both flanks, parked at anything that happens. A rooftop mast on the studio at Weare Point that is visible from most of the town.
brands.says: Meridian is big enough to be part of a region and small enough to be its third story. The town appears on Coastway when something has gone wrong at the docks.
brands.neverConfuse: Any real regional franchise of the era. The name, the idents and the programme titles are invented, and no real presenter, logo or jingle appears.

brands.name: Mickey's
brands.register: Mickey's. Never the Mickey's, never the full name of whoever Mickey was.
brands.physical: Etched glass, a carpet that has given up, a bell nobody rings. Sign hand-painted and repainted a shade off each time.
brands.says: The room where the town's memory is actually kept. Canon: this name is fixed.
brands.neverConfuse: Any real public house. Recorded from canon.md, not invented in this batch.

brands.name: the Tivoli
brands.register: the Tivoli. Going to the pictures, not going to the cinema.
brands.physical: A single screen behind a frontage built for three times the audience it gets. Plastic letters on a rail, some missing, changed on Thursdays.
brands.says: A grand thing the town cannot quite afford to keep. Canon: this name is fixed.
brands.neverConfuse: Tivoli is a widely used cinema name; here it is always the Tivoli, lower-case article, in Meridian. Recorded from canon.md.

brands.name: Meridian Harbour Board
brands.register: the Board. Dockers say the Board decided it, meaning something has been done to them.
brands.physical: Blue and white enamel signage on gates, cranes and the weighbridge. Notices in a glass case by the dock office, drawing-pinned and curling. A crest on letterhead and on the side of every vehicle.
brands.says: The harbour is governed by people who are not from the harbour. Canon: this name is fixed.
brands.neverConfuse: Harbour boards are a real category of British body; this one is invented and no real board's crest, wording or officers appear.

brands.name: Meridian Ferry
brands.register: the ferry. The boat, if you work on it.
brands.physical: One vessel, white over black, a funnel in Board blue. A timetable board at each ramp with the winter service pasted over the summer one. Foot passengers on the upper deck in all weather because the lounge smells of diesel.
brands.says: The town is a crossing point, and the crossing is the thing that has not stopped. Canon: this name is fixed.
brands.neverConfuse: Any real operator. Recorded from canon.md, not invented in this batch.
